title: Fish with Vegetables (carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy)

content.title: About
content.content: The dish combines tender fish (such as cod, salmon or hake) with fresh vegetables: carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale, Swiss chard). It is prepared without potatoes and without tomato‑based sauce, making it light and nutrient‑dense.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fish is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, which support heart and brain health.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for its anti‑cancer properties.
Dark‑green leafy greens are high in vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A for vision.
The combination of fish and vegetables provides a complete set of essential amino acids and micronutrients.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Omega‑3s from fish lower triglycerides and inflammation, while potassium from vegetables helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: Vitamin C from broccoli and beta‑carotene from carrots enhance the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Vision protection
items.content: Beta‑carotene and lutein from carrots and broccoli protect the retina from oxidative stress.

items.title: Reduced risk of chronic disease
items.content: Antioxidants and phytochemicals in the vegetables together with omega‑3s lower the risk of diabetes and certain cancers.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species can contain mercury or cadmium; choosing smaller species and limiting frequency reduces exposure.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions of broccoli may cause gas in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fish can be baked, poached, or steamed, while vegetables are best lightly sautéed or steamed to retain crunch and nutrients. Combine them on a plate, drizzle with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh fish in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for up to 2 days, and store vegetables in the crisper drawer at 4‑6 °C for up to 5 days. For freezing, pack fish in airtight bags and blanch vegetables before freezing; they keep well for up to 3 months.
